title: Click Polls and Online Reviews
objective: After this level you can explain why polls where people choose to take part measure who cares most, not what most people think.
summary: When people choose whether to take part, a poll measures who cares most. Opt-in polls have no margin of error, and online ratings form a J because extreme opinions post.

cards.headline: "Vote now!" Thousands click. What have you learned?
cards.body: Mostly, who felt like clicking. When people choose for themselves whether to take part, a poll stops measuring what most people think. It starts measuring who cares most.

cards.headline: Picking yourself
cards.body: In a self-selected, or opt-in, poll, people choose themselves: a website button, a call-in line. Nobody knows each person's chance of being included, so the results may not represent anyone but the people who joined. That's why Pew won't base its polls on volunteers: they'd likely be more politically interested and engaged than the average American.

cards.headline: Why ratings look like a J
cards.body: Online reviews are opt-in polls too. Product ratings often pile up at 5 stars, with a smaller heap at 1 star and few in between: a J shape. Buyers with extreme opinions are likelier to write a review to "brag or moan" than those who thought it was fine. When researchers had everyone rate the same product, the ratings formed a single hump instead.

cards.fact: No random sample, no margin of error.
cards.context: A margin of error applies only when everyone had a known chance of being picked. Opt-in polls don't qualify, however many clicks pile up. So ask Level 10's question: out of what? For a click poll, the honest answer is out of the people who chose to answer.

options.rationale: That's a random sample, the opposite.

questions.prompt: Online product ratings form a J shape. Match each part of the scale with how many ratings it gets.

questions.prompt: A click poll says 80% back an idea. Asking Level 10's "out of what?", the honest answer is:

options.label: Out of all adults in the country
options.rationale: Only people who chose to click are counted.

options.label: Out of 100 typical voters
options.rationale: A percent is out of 100, but of whom? Of the clickers.

options.label: Out of the people who chose to click

questions.explanation: A share compares a part with a whole. In a click poll, the whole is only the people who chose to answer.
